content:
What is the preferred way of saying that a subgroup (say) is finite?

  • Finite (CommGroup.torsion G) (taking the torsion subgroup as an example)
  • Set.Finite (CommGroup.torsion G : Set G)
  • something else?
    The first two are defeq, so maybe it doesn't really make a big difference, but it would be good to know if there is a "normal form" one should use.

I guess it really depends on your purpose. Both ways you mentioned are used in the existing library. e.g. the first one is used for typeclass instances Subgroup.instFiniteSubtypeMem and the second one is used in Subgroup.orderOf_le_card
As simp is not tagged to Set.finite_coe_iff I would guess that there is no simp normal form in this case.

So far, the final statement is a leaf theorem (finiteness of the torsion subgroup of the group of rational points on an elliptic curve over a number field), so it is not so clear what might be more convenient. Currently, I'm using the first version, so maybe I just leave it like this for now.
Because then it will match the way finiteness is stated in the rest of the group theory library.
